bull_bear.body:
- Income-tax search and seizure exposure — Assessment orders received in the last week of March 2026 for AY 2019-20 to AY 2025-26, following a November 2024 search, raised an aggregate demand; the Company has appealed the outstanding balance, and the Board considers it not sustainable, but the appeal outcome is a pending contingency.
- Working capital and lender reporting discrepancies — The statutory auditors' CARO annexure noted that quarterly returns/statements filed with banks/financial institutions for working capital limits above ₹5 crore were not in agreement with the Company's books of account for quarters during the year, indicating a reconciliation control gap between lender reporting and books.
- Regulatory compliance transition risk (SME to Main Board LODR) — The Company became subject for the first time to Main Board SEBI (LODR) provisions after paid-up capital crossed ₹25 crore in January 2026; the transition already produced one lapse (delayed Q3 FY26 results submission and an NSE fine), evidencing execution risk as governance and reporting systems scale up.
- Change in depreciation method affecting reported profitability — A change from Written Down Value to Straight Line Method for Property, Plant and Equipment depreciation (effective 1 January 2026) was flagged as a Key Audit Matter, given the judgement involved and its effect of lowering depreciation expense and raising profit before tax for the year.
- Revenue recognition judgement on construction contracts — Flagged as a Key Audit Matter due to the estimates and judgement involved in measuring contract revenue and contract costs on a stage-of-completion basis, which is inherent to EPC/construction-contract accounting.
- Geographic concentration in Gujarat — The Company's EPC operations are described as primarily servicing real estate developers, institutions and corporates across Gujarat (Ahmedabad, Gandhinagar, GIFT City, Rajkot and Baroda), indicating concentration in a single state.

outlook.body: The Company expanded its equipment base during the year, which along with higher working capital deployed against an enlarged order book, drove higher finance costs and depreciation. The Company deploys modern construction techniques and equipment, including imported aluminium monolithic formwork systems, PERI systems and captive ready-mix concrete facilities, together with digital project monitoring and enterprise resource planning tools.

outlook.body:
- The moderation in profitability, notwithstanding revenue growth, is attributed to higher finance costs and depreciation from the expansion of the Company's equipment base and a larger quantum of working capital deployed in executing an enlarged order book, together with elevated input and labour costs during the year.
- The order book of the Company stood at approximately ₹725 Crores as at 31st March, 2026, providing revenue visibility over the next 24 to 36 months.
